covers.prompt: Create an entirely original square music album sleeve for an invented band. A finished album cover, edge to edge, not a record mockup, not a poster on a wall. Professional art direction, one striking large subject and strong tonal separation, readable composition even at 40 pixels. Quiet psychedelic atmosphere fitting a lava-lamp evening. No reference to any existing album, artist, trademark, or brand; no borrowed artwork; no watermark. Only the two specified lines of invented artist/album text, correctly spelled. Keep the typography crisp and deliberately composed; leave the central subject unobstructed. Subject: one enormous glowing amber-orange flower growing from a dark volcanic ridge, its broad translucent sculptural petals like molten wax, a slender black stem rising from the ridge at the lower edge. The bloom occupies most of the center, backlit like a small sun, against a flat very dark oxblood sky. Art medium: tactile photographic collage with restrained fine film grain and lithographic warmth; dramatic but simple, no tiny busy details. Palette: near-black burgundy, burnt orange, bright honey amber, small cream highlights. Place large cream elegant serif lettering "HEAT RISES" across the upper margin, and smaller widely spaced cream capitals "THE PARAFFINS" across the lower margin. A bold, organic, memorable indie psychedelic sleeve.
